label: Institution
name: Adjara State Museum
summary:
The Adjara State Museum (Georgian: აჭარის სახელმწიფო მუზეუმი) in Batumi, Adjara (Autonomous Republic of Adjara, Georgia) — houses the primary collection of historical, archaeological, and natural history materials from Adjara, the Black Sea coastal region of southwestern Georgia with a unique history as a Georgian Muslim-majority region that was part of the Ottoman Empire until 1878 and retains distinctive cultural characteristics blending Georgian Orthodox and Ottoman-Muslim heritage.

Adjara's historical complexity — Georgian Orthodox Christian roots, Ottoman rule from 1614 to 1878, Russian imperial incorporation after the 1878 Russo-Turkish War, Soviet Autonomous Republic status from 1921, and current status as an Autonomous Republic within Georgia — created a rich archaeological and historical heritage that the Adjara State Museum preserves. The museum's collections include materials from the ancient Colchis kingdom (home of the Golden Fleece legend), medieval Georgian Christian churches, Ottoman-era artifacts, and Soviet-era items.

Batumi's position as the Black Sea terminus of the Baku-Batumi oil pipeline (built 1883) made it one of the first oil export terminals in history — a crucial node in the global oil economy even before the 20th century's petroleum era. The Adjara State Museum's historical collections document this remarkable convergence of ancient mythology (Colchis/Golden Fleece), medieval Christianity, Ottoman-Muslim culture, and modern industrial oil infrastructure in a single coastal region.
